sanskrit: ata ūrdhvam amātyānāṃ parīkṣeta guṇāguṇān saṃyatātmā kṛtaprajño bhūtikāmaś ca bhūmipaḥ
english: Thereafter the king, self-restrained, mature in wisdom, and desirous of prosperity, should examine the merits and faults of his ministers.

sanskrit: saṃbaddhāḥ puruṣair āptair abhijātaiḥ svadeśajaiḥ ahāryair avyabhīcāraiḥ sarvataḥ suparīkṣitaiḥ
english: He should bind to himself trustworthy men of good birth, native to his own land, incorruptible, never wavering in loyalty, and well tested in every respect.

sanskrit: yodhāḥ srauvās tathā maulās tathaivānye 'py avaskṛtāḥ kartavyā bhūtikāmena puruṣeṇa bubhūṣatā
english: Warriors, hereditary retainers, and others duly equipped should be enlisted by a man who desires prosperity and seeks to flourish.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ vainayikī buddhiḥ prakṛtā caiva śobhanā tejo dhairyaṃ kṣamā śaucam anurāga sthitir dhṛtiḥ
english: Those whose minds are schooled in discipline and whose nature is excellent, who possess energy, steadiness, forbearance, purity, devotion, constancy, and firmness—

sanskrit: parīkṣitaguṇān nityaṃ prauḍhabhāvān dhuraṃdharān pañcopadhāvyatītāṃś ca kuryād rājārthakāriṇaḥ
english: those of tested virtues, of seasoned character, able to bear the yoke of office, and proven against the five temptations—these the king should make the agents of his affairs.

sanskrit: paryāptavacanān vīrān pratipattiviśāradān kulīnān satyasaṃpannān iṅgitajñān aniṣṭhurān
english: Men ample in speech, valiant, skilled in resolve, well-born, endowed with truth, able to read intentions, and free from harshness;

sanskrit: deśakālavidhānajñān bhartṛkāryahitaiṣiṇaḥ nityam artheṣu sarveṣu rājā kurvīta mantriṇaḥ
english: who know the disposition of place and time and seek the welfare of their master's work—such men the king should ever make his counselors in all matters.

sanskrit: hīnatejā hy asaṃhṛṣṭo naiva jātu vyavasyati avaśyaṃ janayaty eva sarvakarmasu saṃśayān
english: For a man wanting in energy and joyless never reaches a firm decision, but inevitably breeds doubts in all undertakings.

sanskrit: evam alpaśruto mantrī kalyāṇābhijano 'py uta dharmārthakāmayukto 'pi nālaṃ mantraṃ parīkṣitum
english: Likewise a counselor of little learning, though of auspicious birth and versed in dharma, artha, and kāma, is not competent to weigh counsel.

sanskrit: tathaivānabhijāto 'pi kāmam astu bahuśrutaḥ anāyaka ivācakṣur muhyaty ūhyeṣu karmasu
english: And so one not nobly born, though he be ever so widely learned, falters in matters that call for reasoning, like a leaderless man without eyes.

sanskrit: yo vā hy asthirasaṃkalpo buddhimān āgatāgamaḥ upāyajño 'pi nālaṃ sa karma yāpayituṃ ciram
english: And he who is unsteady of purpose, though intelligent, learned in tradition, and skilled in expedients, is unable to carry an undertaking through to its end.

sanskrit: kevalāt punar ācārāt karmaṇo nopapadyate parimarśo viśeṣāṇām aśrutasyeha durmateḥ
english: From mere routine conduct, again, no discernment of the finer points of an affair can arise in the unlearned man of poor understanding.

sanskrit: mantriṇy ananurakte tu viśvāso na hi vidyate tasmād ananuraktāya naiva mantraṃ prakāśayet
english: In a counselor who lacks devotion there can be no trust; therefore one should never disclose counsel to a man who is not devoted.

sanskrit: vyathayed dhi sa rājānaṃ mantribhiḥ sahito 'nṛjuḥ mārutopahatacchidraiḥ praviśyāgnir iva drumam
english: For a crooked man, joined with other counselors, would torment the king, as fire entering through the fissures opened by the wind consumes a tree.

sanskrit: saṃkrudhyaty ekadā svāmī sthānāc caivāpakarṣati vācā kṣipati saṃrabdhas tataḥ paścāt prasīdati
english: A master grows wroth at times and casts a man down from his post; in his fury he assails him with words, yet afterward he is appeased.

sanskrit: tāni tāny anuraktena śakyāny anutitikṣitum mantriṇāṃ ca bhavet krodho visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ
english: All such things can be endured by a devoted man; but a counselor's wrath would burst forth like the crash of a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: yas tu saṃharate tāni bhartuḥ priyacikīrṣayā samānasukhaduḥkhaṃ taṃ pṛcched artheṣu mānavam
english: But the man who restrains such resentments, wishing only to please his master, and who shares alike in his joys and sorrows—him the king should consult in his affairs.

sanskrit: anṛjus tv anurakto 'pi saṃpannaś cetarair guṇaiḥ rājñaḥ prajñānayukto 'pi na mantraṃ śrotum arhati
english: But a crooked man, though devoted and endowed with all other virtues and gifted with discernment of the king's mind, does not deserve to hear his counsel.

sanskrit: yo 'mitraiḥ saha saṃbaddho na paurān bahu manyate sa suhṛt tādṛśo rājño na mantraṃ śrotum arhati
english: He who is bound up with the king's enemies and holds the townsfolk in little regard—such a friend of the king does not deserve to hear his counsel.

sanskrit: avidvān aśuciḥ stabdhaḥ śatrusevī vikatthanaḥ sa suhṛt krodhano lubdho na mantraṃ śrotum arhati
english: The ignorant, the impure, the arrogant, the server of foes, the boaster, the irascible, the greedy friend—he does not deserve to hear the counsel.

sanskrit: āgantuś cānurakto 'pi kāmam astu bahuśrutaḥ satkṛtaḥ saṃvibhakto vā na mantraṃ śrotum arhati
english: And a stranger, though devoted and ever so learned, though honored or made a sharer in fortune, does not deserve to hear the counsel.

sanskrit: yas tv alpenāpi kāryeṇa sakṛd ākṣārito bhavet punar anyair guṇair yukto na mantraṃ śrotum arhati
english: And he who, even over some trifling matter, has once been reproached, though afterward endowed with other virtues, does not deserve to hear the counsel.

sanskrit: kṛtaprajñaś ca medhāvī budho jānapadaḥ śuciḥ sarvakarmasu yaḥ śuddhaḥ sa mantraṃ śrotum arhati
english: The man mature in wisdom, intelligent, wise, native to the realm, pure, and unblemished in all his dealings—he deserves to hear the counsel.

sanskrit: jñānavijñānasaṃpannaḥ prakṛtijñaḥ parātmanoḥ suhṛd ātmasamo rājñaḥ sa mantraṃ śrotum arhati
english: Endowed with knowledge and discernment, knowing the nature of foe and self alike, a friend who is the king's very equal—he deserves to hear the counsel.

sanskrit: satyavāk śīlasaṃpanno gambhīraḥ satrapo mṛduḥ pitṛpaitāmaho yaḥ syāt sa mantraṃ śrotum arhati
english: Truthful in speech, endowed with good character, deep, modest, and gentle, one who is a servant from his fathers and forefathers—he deserves to hear the counsel.

sanskrit: saṃtuṣṭaḥ saṃmataḥ satyaḥ śauṭīro dveṣyapāpakaḥ mantravit kālavic chūraḥ sa mantraṃ śrotum arhati
english: Content, esteemed, truthful, high-spirited, holder of evil-doers in hatred, knower of counsel and of the right time, and valiant—he deserves to hear the counsel.

sanskrit: sarvalokaṃ samaṃ śaktaḥ sāntvena kurute vaśe tasmai mantraḥ prayoktavyo daṇḍam ādhitsatā nṛpa
english: To one able to bring all people equally under his sway by conciliation, O king, the counsel should be entrusted by him who would wield the rod of punishment.

sanskrit: paurajānapadā yasmin viśvāsaṃ dharmato gatāḥ yoddhā nayavipaścic ca sa mantraṃ śrotum arhati
english: He in whom the townsfolk and country-folk place their trust by virtue of his righteousness, a warrior and one wise in statecraft—he deserves to hear the counsel.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarvair guṇair etair upapannāḥ supūjitāḥ mantriṇaḥ prakṛtijñāḥ syus tryavarā mahad īpsavaḥ
english: Therefore the counselors, well honored and endowed with all these virtues and knowing the affairs of state, should number at least three, if one aspires to greatness.

sanskrit: svāsu prakṛtiṣu chidraṃ lakṣayeran parasya ca mantriṇo mantramūlaṃ hi rājño rāṣṭraṃ vivardhate
english: They should mark the weak points in their own constituents and in those of the foe; for it is upon counsel as its root that the king's realm grows and prospers.

sanskrit: nāsya chidraṃ paraḥ paśyec chidreṣu param anviyāt gūhet kūrma ivāṅgāni rakṣed vivaram ātmanaḥ
english: Let no enemy see his weak point; let him watch for the foe's weak points; let him hide his limbs like a tortoise and guard his own openings.

sanskrit: mantragrāhā hi rājyasya mantriṇo ye manīṣiṇaḥ mantrasaṃhanano rājā mantrāṅgānītaro janaḥ
english: The wise counselors are the holders of the kingdom's counsel; the king is the very frame that binds the counsel together, and the rest of the people are its limbs.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ praṇidhimūlaṃ hi mantrasāraṃ pracakṣate svāminaṃ tv anuvartanti vṛttyartham iha mantriṇaḥ
english: They declare that the kingdom is rooted in espionage and has counsel for its essence; and here the counselors follow their master for the sake of their livelihood.

sanskrit: sa vinīya madakrodhau mānam īrṣyāṃ ca nirvṛtaḥ nityaṃ pañcopadhātītair mantrayet saha mantribhiḥ
english: Having subdued pride and anger, conceit and envy, and grown serene, he should ever take counsel together with ministers proven against the five temptations.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ vividhaṃ vimarśaṃ; budhyeta cittaṃ viniveśya tatra svaniścayaṃ taṃ paraniścayaṃ ca; nivedayed uttaramantrakāle
english: Fixing his mind upon it, he should grasp the manifold deliberation of those three; and at the time of further counsel he should set forth both his own conclusion and that of the others.

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmajñam upetya pṛcched; yukto guruṃ brāhmaṇam uttamārtham niṣṭhā kṛtā tena yadā saha syāt; taṃ tatra mārgaṃ praṇayed asaktam
english: Composed, he should approach and consult a venerable brāhmaṇa learned in dharma, artha, and kāma upon the highest matter; and when a firm resolve has been reached with him, he should pursue that course without attachment.

sanskrit: evaṃ sadā mantrayitavyam āhur; ye mantratattvārthaviniścayajñāḥ tasmāt tvam evaṃ praṇayeḥ sadaiva; mantraṃ prajāsaṃgrahaṇe samartham
english: Thus, they say—those who know how to determine the true meaning of counsel—should one ever take counsel; therefore you too should always so frame counsel fit to win and hold the people.

sanskrit: na vāmanāḥ kubjakṛśā na khañjā; nāndhā jaḍāḥ strī na napuṃsakaṃ ca na cātra tiryaṅ na puro na paścān; nordhvaṃ na cādhaḥ pracareta kaś cit
english: Let no dwarf, hunchback, or emaciated man, no cripple, no blind or witless person, no woman or eunuch be there; let no animal, and let no one move about in front or behind, above or below.

sanskrit: āruhya vātāyanam eva śūnyaṃ; sthalaṃ prakāśaṃ kuśakāśahīnam vāgaṅgadoṣān parihṛtya mantraṃ; saṃmantrayet kāryam ahīnakālam
english: Having ascended to an empty terrace, open and bright, free of kuśa and kāśa grass, and avoiding all faults of speech and gesture, he should deliberate his counsel on the matter at no untimely hour.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam bṛhaspateś ca saṃvādaṃ śakrasya ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they cite this ancient tale, the dialogue of Bṛhaspati and Śakra, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca kiṃ svid ekapadaṃ brahman puruṣaḥ samyag ācaran pramāṇaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ yaśaś caivāpnuyān mahat
english: Śakra said: What is that one word, O brāhmaṇa, which a man, practicing rightly, may become the standard for all beings and win great renown?

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca sāntvam ekapadaṃ śakra puruṣaḥ samyag ācaran pramāṇaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ yaśaś caivāpnuyān mahat
english: Bṛhaspati said: Conciliation is that one word, O Śakra, by practicing which rightly a man may become the standard for all beings and win great renown.

sanskrit: etad ekapadaṃ śakra sarvalokasukhāvaham ācaran sarvabhūteṣu priyo bhavati sarvadā
english: This one word, O Śakra, brings happiness to the whole world; practicing it toward all beings, a man becomes dear to them forever.

sanskrit: yo hi nābhāṣate kiṃ cit satataṃ bhrukuṭīmukhaḥ dveṣyo bhavati bhūtānāṃ sa sāntvam iha nācaran
english: For he who never speaks a word, his face forever knit in a frown, becomes hateful to all beings, since he practices no conciliation here.

sanskrit: yas tu pūrvam abhiprekṣya pūrvam evābhibhāṣate smitapūrvābhibhāṣī ca tasya lokaḥ prasīdati
english: But he who first looks kindly upon a man and is the first to address him, speaking with a smile—toward him the world is well disposed.

sanskrit: dānam eva hi sarvatra sāntvenānabhijalpitam na prīṇayati bhūtāni nirvyañjanam ivāśanam
english: For even a gift, given everywhere without kindly words, does not please beings—like food served without seasoning.

sanskrit: adātā hy api bhūtānāṃ madhurām īrayan giram sarvalokam imaṃ śakra sāntvena kurute vaśe
english: For even a man who gives nothing, by uttering sweet speech to beings, brings this whole world under his sway through conciliation, O Śakra.

sanskrit: tasmāt sāntvaṃ prakartavyaṃ daṇḍam ādhitsatām iha phalaṃ ca janayaty evaṃ na cāsyodvijate janaḥ
english: Therefore conciliation should be practiced by those who would wield the rod here; thus it bears fruit, and the people do not shrink from him in dread.

sanskrit: sukṛtasya hi sāntvasya ślakṣṇasya madhurasya ca samyag āsevyamānasya tulyaṃ jātu na vidyate
english: For to conciliation well wrought, smooth and sweet and rightly employed, there is never found an equal.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktaḥ kṛtavān sarvaṃ tathā śakraḥ purodhasā tathā tvam api kaunteya samyag etat samācara
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus instructed by his preceptor, Śakra did all accordingly; and you too, son of Kuntī, should practice this rightly.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ svid iha rājendra pālayan pārthivaḥ prajāḥ prati dharmaṃ viśeṣeṇa kīrtim āpnoti śāśvatīm
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How, O lord of kings, does a sovereign, while protecting his subjects in accordance with dharma, win in particular an everlasting fame?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vyavahāreṇa śuddhena prajāpālanatatparaḥ prāpya dharmaṃ ca kīrtiṃ ca lokāv āpnoty ubhau śuciḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: By pure administration of justice, devoted to the protection of his subjects, the upright king attains both dharma and fame, and wins both worlds.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kīdṛśaṃ vyavahāraṃ tu kaiś ca vyavaharen nṛpaḥ etat pṛṣṭo mahāprājña yathāvad vaktum arhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What sort of justice, and with whose aid, should the king administer? Being asked this, O greatly wise one, you ought to declare it duly.

sanskrit: ye caite pūrvakathitā guṇās te puruṣaṃ prati naikasmin puruṣe hy ete vidyanta iti me matiḥ
english: And those virtues that were earlier spoken of concerning a man—these are not found in any single man, such is my view.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam etan mahāprājña yathā vadasi buddhimān durlabhaḥ puruṣaḥ kaś cid ebhir guṇaguṇair yutaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: It is so, O greatly wise one, as you say, O intelligent one: hard to find is any man endowed with all these manifold virtues.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu saṃkṣepataḥ śīlaṃ prayatne neha durlabham vakṣyāmi tu yathāmātyān yādṛśāṃś ca kariṣyasi
english: Yet good character, in brief, is not hard to find here for one who strives; I shall tell you how, and what manner of ministers you should appoint.

sanskrit: caturo brāhmaṇān vaidyān pragalbhān sāttvikāñ śucīn trīṃś ca śūdrān vinītāṃś ca śucīn karmaṇi pūrvake
english: Four brāhmaṇas, learned, bold, of sattvic temper, and pure; and three śūdras, disciplined and pure, of proven service in their former duties;

sanskrit: aṣṭābhiś ca guṇair yuktaṃ sūtaṃ paurāṇikaṃ caret pañcāśadvarṣavayasaṃ pragalbham anasūyakam
english: and one sūta versed in the ancient lore, endowed with eight virtues, fifty years of age, bold, and free from envy, he should employ;

sanskrit: matismṛtisamāyuktaṃ vinītaṃ samadarśanam kārye vivadamānānāṃ śaktam artheṣv alolupam
english: possessed of intelligence and memory, disciplined, even-handed, competent among litigants disputing a case, and ungreedy of gain.

sanskrit: vivarjitānāṃ vyasanaiḥ sughoraiḥ saptabhir bhṛśam aṣṭānāṃ mantriṇāṃ madhye mantraṃ rājopadhārayet
english: In the midst of these eight counselors, wholly free from the seven dreadful vices, the king should take his counsel.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpreṣayed rāṣṭre rāṣṭrāyātha ca darśayet anena vyavahāreṇa draṣṭavyās te prajāḥ sadā
english: Then he should send them forth into the realm, and make it known to the realm: 'By this administration of justice are your subjects ever to be overseen.'

sanskrit: na cāpi gūḍhaṃ kāryaṃ te grāhyaṃ kāryopaghātakam kārye khalu vipanne tvāṃ so 'dharmas tāṃś ca pīḍayet
english: Nor should any hidden affair, ruinous to the business of state, be entertained by you; for should the affair miscarry, that unrighteousness would afflict both you and them.

sanskrit: vidravec caiva rāṣṭraṃ te śyenāt pakṣigaṇā iva parisravec ca satataṃ naur viśīrṇeva sāgare
english: And your realm would scatter, like flocks of birds fleeing a hawk, and would forever leak away like a shattered boat upon the sea.

sanskrit: prajāḥ pālayato 'samyag adharmeṇeha bhūpateḥ hārdaṃ bhayaṃ saṃbhavati svargaś cāsya virudhyate
english: For a king who protects his subjects wrongly and unrighteously here, a fear arises within his very heart, and heaven is barred against him.

sanskrit: atha yo 'dharmataḥ pāti rājāmātyo 'tha vātmajaḥ dharmāsane niyuktaḥ san dharmamūlaṃ nararṣabha
english: And whoever rules unrighteously—be he king, minister, or king's son—when appointed to the seat of justice that is rooted in dharma, O bull among men—

sanskrit: kāryeṣv adhikṛtāḥ samyag akurvanto nṛpānugāḥ ātmānaṃ purataḥ kṛtvā yānty adhaḥ sahapārthivāḥ
english: the king's followers, appointed over affairs but not discharging them aright, go down to ruin, putting themselves at the head, together with the king.

sanskrit: balātkṛtānāṃ balibhiḥ kṛpaṇaṃ bahu jalpatām nātho vai bhūmipo nityam anāthānāṃ nṛṇāṃ bhavet
english: Of those oppressed by the powerful and crying out piteously in their misery, the king is ever the protector—the protector of men who have no other lord.

sanskrit: tataḥ sākṣibalaṃ sādhu dvaidhe vādakṛtaṃ bhavet asākṣikam anāthaṃ vā parīkṣyaṃ tad viśeṣataḥ
english: In a dispute, then, the weight of good witnesses must decide the matter; but a case without witnesses, or one unsupported, must be examined with particular care.

sanskrit: aparādhānurūpaṃ ca daṇḍaṃ pāpeṣu pātayet udvejayed dhanair ṛddhān daridrān vadhabandhanaiḥ
english: He should lay upon evildoers a punishment befitting the offense: the wealthy he should chasten with fines, the poor with flogging and imprisonment.

sanskrit: vinayair api durvṛttān prahārair api pārthivaḥ sāntvenopapradānena śiṣṭāṃś ca paripālayet
english: The wicked the king may discipline, even with corrective measures and with blows; and the well-behaved he should cherish with conciliation and with gifts.

sanskrit: rājño vadhaṃ cikīrṣed yas tasya citro vadho bhavet ājīvakasya stenasya varṇasaṃkarakasya ca
english: Whoever should seek to slay the king—for him let the death be exemplary; so too for the assassin, the thief, and the corrupter of the social order.

sanskrit: samyak praṇayato daṇḍaṃ bhūmipasya viśāṃ pate yuktasya vā nāsty adharmo dharma eveha śāśvataḥ
english: For a king who duly metes out punishment, O lord of the people, or for one fit to do so, there is no unrighteousness; here it is righteousness everlasting.

sanskrit: kāmakāreṇa daṇḍaṃ tu yaḥ kuryād avicakṣaṇaḥ sa ihākīrtisaṃyukto mṛto narakam āpnuyāt
english: But the unwise man who inflicts punishment at the prompting of caprice becomes joined to infamy here, and when dead attains hell.

sanskrit: na parasya śravād eva pareṣāṃ daṇḍam arpayet āgamānugamaṃ kṛtvā badhnīyān mokṣayeta vā
english: He should not inflict punishment upon others merely on another's word; having pursued the proper inquiry, he should then either imprison or release them.

sanskrit: na tu hanyān nṛpo jātu dūtaṃ kasyāṃ cid āpadi dūtasya hantā nirayam āviśet sacivaiḥ saha
english: But a king should never slay an envoy in any extremity; the slayer of an envoy enters into hell together with his ministers.

sanskrit: yathoktavādinaṃ dūtaṃ kṣatradharmarato nṛpaḥ yo hanyāt pitaras tasya bhrūṇahatyām avāpnuyuḥ
english: A king devoted to the kṣatriya's dharma who slays an envoy for delivering his message as told—the forefathers of such a king incur the guilt of slaying an embryo.

sanskrit: kulīnaḥ śīlasaṃpanno vāgmī dakṣaḥ priyaṃvadaḥ yathoktavādī smṛtimān dūtaḥ syāt saptabhir guṇaiḥ
english: Well-born, endowed with good character, eloquent, skillful, agreeable in speech, faithful in delivering his message, and of good memory—an envoy should possess these seven virtues.

sanskrit: etair eva guṇair yuktaḥ pratīhāro 'sya rakṣitā śirorakṣaś ca bhavati guṇair etaiḥ samanvitaḥ
english: Endowed with these same virtues, his door-warden becomes his protector; and possessed of these same virtues, one becomes the guardian of his very head.

sanskrit: dharmārthaśāstratattvajñaḥ saṃdhivigrahako bhavet matimān dhṛtimān dhīmān rahasyavinigūhitā
english: One who knows the true import of the treatises on dharma and artha should be the minister of peace and war—intelligent, resolute, wise, and a keeper of secrets.

sanskrit: kulīnaḥ satyasaṃpannaḥ śakto 'mātyaḥ praśaṃsitaḥ etair eva guṇair yuktas tathā senāpatir bhavet
english: Well-born, endowed with truth, capable—such is the praiseworthy minister; and endowed with these same virtues, so too should the commander of the army be.
